name: inprocess-obi-axil-uart-zipdma-route-read-f1f6
description: One Ibex RVFI OBI CPU with one real AXI4-Lite ZipCPU UART and a ZipDMA: the master reads the fixed UART SETUP register through the target's own AR/R channels and writes the captured word into an incrementing RAM block.

evidence.source: the same pinned wbuart register file behind the AXI4-Lite slave: third_party/soc-zipcpu-wbuart/rtl/wbuart.v:119-137,513

notes: the routed AXI4-Lite read is one AR/R pair per beat: the master presents the fixed SETUP address four times, each read returns the word the F4 case stored, and the captured words land in the incrementing RAM destination block

the routed target is the pinned ZipCPU axiluart AXI4-Lite slave behind the generated axi4_lite_mmio_bridge; the host presents the routed beat on the same generic request port the CPU's own MMIO uses, and the bridge drives AW/W/B or AR/R and returns the slave's R data as the beat's response
the target is mapped at 0x20006000 rather than its SoC 0x40000000 because the pinned ZipDMA's SOURCE/DESTINATION CSR fields are 30-bit byte addresses: a byte address >= 0x40000000 cannot be encoded
rx=1 and cts_n=0 are the same pin constants the F2/F4 AXI4-Lite scenario declares for this slave; SETUP 0 (rw), FIFO_STATUS 4 (ro), RXREG 8 (rw) and TXREG 12 (rw) are the four declared registers
F4 stores the source word in SETUP first (0x20006000), then F6 reads it back through the DMA; a read route does not reset the devices
